title: Project Management Principles - Module 3: Time & Cost Management
subtitle: Comprehensive exam preparation quiz covering CPM, PERT, Gantt charts, and Earned Value Management

questions.question: What is the primary challenge for a project manager according to the module?
options: Meeting the deadline and the cost
questions.explanation: The module explicitly states that the biggest challenge for a project manager is meeting the deadline and the cost.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a core activity in the project time management process?
questions.explanation: The core activities listed in the module are: definition of activities, scheduling activities, resource estimate, estimated duration, preparation of the plan, and control of the plan.

questions.question: What is a milestone in project management?
options: A task that takes one day to complete
A very important event that has no duration and is used to monitor project progress
questions.explanation: According to the module, a milestone is a very important event that has no duration and is used to monitor the progress of the project.

questions.question: What is the purpose of sequencing in project management?
options: To establish a logical sequence between network activities
questions.explanation: Sequencing is the establishment of a logical sequence between network activities. It ensures that all necessary steps happen correctly and helps optimize resources efficiently.

questions.question: Which dependency relationship allows activities to start before their predecessors finish?
questions.explanation: Start to Start (SS) dependency allows activities to begin before their predecessors are complete. Both can start at the same time.

questions.question: In the Finish to Finish dependency, what constraint exists?
options: The successor cannot start until the predecessor finishes
The successor cannot finish until the predecessor finishes
Both activities must have the same duration
The successor must start before the predecessor
questions.explanation: In Finish to Finish (FF) dependency, the successor cannot finish until the predecessor finishes. Example: editing cannot finish until the first draft is finished.

questions.question: What does the Start to Finish dependency represent?
questions.explanation: Start to Finish (SF) dependency means the successor cannot finish until the predecessor starts. Example: old app version stays live until new version starts running.

questions.question: When was the PERT network technique created and by whom?
questions.explanation: PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) was created in 1958 at the request of the US Navy.

questions.question: What is the primary focus of PERT?
options: The notions of flow and dependencies
questions.explanation: PERT focuses on the notions of flow and dependencies and determines the critical path.

questions.question: What is the PERT formula for estimating activity duration?
questions.explanation: The PERT formula is (P + 4M + O) / 6, where P is pessimistic, M is most likely, and O is optimistic time.

questions.question: In the PERT formula, what does 'O' represent?
questions.explanation: O represents Optimistic Time, the best-case scenario or minimum amount of time an activity might take.

questions.question: What does 'P' represent in the PERT formula?
questions.explanation: P represents Pessimistic Time, the worst-case scenario or maximum amount of time an activity might take.

questions.question: Using the PERT formula with P=16 days, M=10 days, O=8 days, what is the estimated duration?
What is the Critical Path Method (CPM)?
options: A project management technique used to plan, schedule, and manage projects
questions.explanation: CPM is a project management technique used to plan, schedule, and manage projects by identifying the critical path.

questions.question: What is the critical path in a project network?
options: The shortest path through the network
The path with the most activities
The sequence of tasks that must be completed on time to ensure project completion
The path with the highest cost
questions.explanation: The critical path is the sequence of tasks that must be completed on time to ensure the project is completed as scheduled. It is the longest path and cannot be delayed.

questions.question: What is the float (slack) time in the Critical Path Method?
options: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without affecting project completion
questions.explanation: Float or slack time is the amount of time that an activity can be delayed without affecting the project's completion time.

questions.question: How is total float calculated in CPM?
questions.explanation: Total float is calculated as: Latest Start - Earliest Start, or alternatively, Latest End - Earliest End.

questions.question: What does ES (Earliest Start) represent?
options: The latest time an activity can start
Moving forward from start to finish, the earliest time an activity can start
questions.explanation: ES (Earliest Start) is calculated by moving from start to finish. It represents the earliest time an activity can start based on its predecessors.

questions.question: What does LS (Latest Start) represent?
options: The earliest time an activity can start
Moving backward from finish to start, the latest time an activity can start without delaying the project
questions.explanation: LS (Latest Start) is calculated by moving backward from finish to start. It represents the latest time an activity can start without delaying project completion.

questions.question: What is the characteristic of activities on the critical path?
questions.explanation: The critical path is the path where all activities have zero float. These activities cannot be delayed without affecting project completion.

questions.question: What is backtracking in the Critical Path Method?
options: The process to determine the late start or late finish times for activities
questions.explanation: Backtracking is the process to determine the late start or late finish times for activities, working backward from the project end date.

questions.question: What is fast-tracking in project management?
options: Running multiple activities on the critical path in parallel to reduce overall project time
questions.explanation: Fast-tracking is running multiple activities on the critical path in parallel to reduce overall project time. Only possible for activities without hard dependencies.

questions.question: What is crashing in project management?
options: Allocating additional resources to an activity to bring it to completion faster
questions.explanation: Crashing is allocating additional resources to an activity to bring it to completion faster, typically used when there is an early deadline.

questions.question: When should resources be diverted for crashing?
options: From activities on the critical path
questions.explanation: Resources should be diverted from high-float tasks (non-critical activities) for crashing, not from activities on the critical path.

questions.question: What is a Gantt chart?
options: A network diagram showing task dependencies
A visual representation of a project schedule that displays tasks and their timelines
questions.explanation: A Gantt chart is a visual representation of a project schedule with tasks listed on the left and timeline running horizontally.

questions.question: What information does a Gantt chart display?
questions.explanation: A Gantt chart displays tasks, timescale, dependencies between phases and tasks, and float or slack information.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of using a Gantt chart?
options: User-friendly view and life to the project plan
questions.explanation: Gantt charts provide a user-friendly view and bring life to the project plan, allowing quick visualization of the critical path.

questions.question: When should CPM be used instead of Gantt charts?
options: When you need to track complex task dependencies and want a detailed view
questions.explanation: CPM should be used when you need to track complex task dependencies and want a more detailed view of the project timeline.

questions.question: What are the three types of cost estimates in project management?
options: Rough Order of Magnitude, Budgetary, Final
questions.explanation: The three types are: Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM), Budgetary Estimate, and Final Estimate, each with different accuracy levels.

questions.question: What is the accuracy range of a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) estimate?
questions.explanation: ROM has an accuracy of about ±50%. It is used very early during the initiation phase when very little information is available.

questions.question: When is a Budgetary Estimate typically used?
options: During planning to request approval and define the working budget
questions.explanation: Budgetary Estimate (±10% accuracy) is used during planning to request approval and define the working budget during the authorization phase.

questions.question: What is the accuracy range of a Final Estimate?
questions.explanation: Final Estimate has an accuracy of about ±5% and is used after detailed planning and refined during project execution.

questions.question: What are variable costs in project management?
options: Costs proportional to the amount of work (labor hours, materials, supplies)
questions.explanation: Variable costs are proportional to the amount of work, such as labor hours, materials, and supplies.

questions.question: What are fixed costs in project management?
options: Costs that do not change with volume changes (start-up costs, office rent)
questions.explanation: Fixed costs do not change with volume changes, such as start-up costs, setting up, and renting office space.

questions.question: What are direct costs in project management?
options: Costs directly attributable to project work (team salaries, travel, awards)
questions.explanation: Direct costs are directly attributable to the work of the project, such as travel of team members, recognition awards, and team salaries.

questions.question: What are indirect costs in project management?
options: Overheads or costs incurred for the benefit of more than one project (taxes, utilities, marketing)
questions.explanation: Indirect costs are overheads or costs incurred for the benefit of more than one project, such as taxes, social security, and electricity.

questions.question: What is the Earned Value Management (EVM) technique?
options: A project performance management technique that considers content, time, and cost elements
questions.explanation: EVM is a project performance management technique that takes into account content, time, and cost elements and compares actual situation versus baseline.

questions.question: What does PV (Planned Value) represent in EVM?
options: The budgeted amount to complete an activity
questions.explanation: PV (Planned Value) is the budgeted amount to complete an activity. It is the project's budget or cumulative budget for an activity at a given time.

questions.question: What does AC (Actual Cost) represent in EVM?
options: The actual cost to perform the work or costs incurred on the project
questions.explanation: AC (Actual Cost) is the actual cost to perform the work or costs incurred on the project.

questions.question: What does EV (Earned Value) represent in EVM?
options: The amount of budgeted work actually done for a task in a given period
questions.explanation: EV (Earned Value) is the amount of budgeted work actually done for a task in a given period, calculated as: Planned Value × percentage of completion.

questions.question: What does BCWS represent in EVM terminology?
questions.explanation: BCWS (Budgeted Cost of Work Scheduled) is equivalent to PV (Planned Value).

questions.question: What does BCWP represent in EVM terminology?
questions.explanation: BCWP (Budgeted Cost of Work Performed) is equivalent to EV (Earned Value).

questions.question: What does ACWP represent in EVM terminology?
questions.explanation: ACWP (Actual Cost of Work Performed) is equivalent to AC (Actual Cost).

questions.question: What is the Cost Variance (CV) formula in EVM?
questions.explanation: CV (Cost Variance) = BCWP - ACWP. It indicates whether the project is under or over budget at a specific point in time.

questions.question: What is the Schedule Variance (SV) formula in EVM?
questions.explanation: SV (Schedule Variance) = BCWP - BCWS. It helps determine whether the project is ahead of, on, or behind schedule.

questions.question: What does a negative Cost Variance indicate?
questions.explanation: A negative CV indicates that BCWP < ACWP, meaning the project is over budget (spending more than planned).

questions.question: What does a negative Schedule Variance indicate?
questions.explanation: A negative SV indicates that BCWP < BCWS, meaning the project is behind schedule (less work completed than planned).

questions.question: What is the Cost Performance Index (CPI) formula?
questions.explanation: CPI (Cost Performance Index) = BCWP / ACWP. It represents the efficiency of resource use.

questions.question: What is the Schedule Performance Index (SPI) formula?
questions.explanation: SPI (Schedule Performance Index) = BCWP / BCWS. It represents the effectiveness of schedule adherence.

questions.question: What does a CPI less than 1 indicate?
options: Project is cost-inefficient and could exceed budget
questions.explanation: CPI < 1 indicates that the value of work performed is less than the money spent. The project could exceed its budget.

questions.question: What does an SPI less than 1 indicate?
questions.explanation: SPI < 1 indicates that the work done is less than the planned work. The project is behind schedule.

questions.question: In an EVM exercise with Budget 400k€, Duration 4 months, after 3 months with AC=200k€ and EV=100k€, what is the BCWS?
questions.explanation: BCWS = (Budget / Duration) × Months Elapsed = (400k€ / 4) × 3 = 300k€

questions.question: In the same EVM exercise, what is the Cost Variance (CV)?
questions.explanation: CV = BCWP - ACWP = 100k€ - 200k€ = -100k€ (over budget)

questions.question: In the same EVM exercise, what is the Schedule Variance (SV)?
questions.explanation: SV = BCWP - BCWS = 100k€ - 300k€ = -200k€ (behind schedule)

questions.question: In the same EVM exercise, what is the CPI?
questions.explanation: CPI = BCWP / ACWP = 100k€ / 200k€ = 0.5 (50% cost-inefficient)

questions.question: In the same EVM exercise, what is the SPI?
questions.explanation: SPI = BCWP / BCWS = 100k€ / 300k€ = 0.33 (33% schedule-ineffective)

questions.question: What is the Law of Diminishing Returns in project management?
options: Adding more resources always speeds up tasks
It is not by adding twice as many resources that one can accomplish a task at half the time
questions.explanation: The Law of Diminishing Returns states that it is not by adding twice as many resources for a task that one can accomplish this task at half the time.

questions.question: What is Value Analysis (Value Engineering) in cost management?
options: Looking for less expensive ways to do the same job with the same content
questions.explanation: Value Analysis is looking for less expensive ways to do the same job with the same content.

questions.question: What is a contingency reserve in project budgeting?
options: Extra funds for known unknowns (known risks)
Extra funds for unknown unknowns (unforeseen circumstances)
questions.explanation: Contingency reserve covers known unknowns (known risks) and is included in the baseline.

questions.question: What is a management reserve in project budgeting?
options: Additional funds to cover unforeseen circumstances or certain changes
questions.explanation: Management reserve is additional funds to cover unforeseen circumstances or certain changes (unknown unknowns).

questions.question: What is an S-curve in project management?
options: A visual representation of a project's financial performance over time
questions.explanation: S-curve analysis offers a clear visual representation of a project's financial performance over time to monitor costs, identify variances, and make informed decisions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of project control in time management?
options: To monitor progress, identify variances, and manage alerts
questions.explanation: Project control involves periodic progress reports, various performance measures, planning for the unexpected, and alert management in case of problems.

questions.question: What is the difference between efficiency and effectiveness in project management?
options: Efficiency optimizes resource use; effectiveness ensures project goals are met
Effectiveness is more important than efficiency
Efficiency is about time; effectiveness is about cost
questions.explanation: Efficiency helps optimize resource use, while effectiveness ensures that the project is focused on the right goals and achieves meaningful results.

questions.question: What is a network diagram in project management?
options: A schematic display of relationships between project activities
questions.explanation: A network diagram is a schematic display of the relationships between project activities, always drawn from left to right to reflect the order of the project.

questions.question: What is the main difference between PERT and CPM?
options: PERT is for small projects; CPM is for large projects
PERT assumes uncertainty; CPM assumes certainty
PERT is cheaper; CPM is more expensive
PERT is faster; CPM is slower
questions.explanation: PERT assumes tasks are uncertain and uses probability distribution; CPM assumes tasks are well-defined and can be scheduled with certainty.

questions.question: What should be considered when estimating activity duration?
options: Level of difficulty, organization experience, and resource availability
questions.explanation: To estimate duration, consider: level of difficulty, organization experience in execution, and availability and experience of necessary resources.

questions.question: What is the iterative process in duration estimation?
options: Modifying estimates over time to be closer to reality
questions.explanation: The iterative process involves modifying estimates over time to be closer to reality as more information becomes available.
